title: Transport of the right-adjoint mate across a source scheme isomorphism
statement: Let P,U,S,T be quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, f:P→S and f′:U→S be qcqs morphisms, e:U≅P satisfy e.hom followed by f equals f′, and g:T→S be any morphism. Choose right adjoints a,b,d,b′ with adjunctions to the canonical lifted direct images of f,f′, pullback(f,g)→T and pullback(f′,g)→T, respectively. Suppose ordinary base change for f′ along g is invertible on every object of D_QCoh(U). Fix K in D_QCoh(S), and let r:pullback(f′,g)→pullback(f,g) satisfy the projection equations. For every family hβf asserting invertibility of ordinary base change for f on D_QCoh(P), the ambient second mate for f at K pulled back along r is isomorphic in the arrow category to the ambient second mate for f′ at K. No invertibility of the second mates is assumed. Schemes, fibre products, derived categories, pullback, direct image, the canonical lifted qcqs direct image, ordinary base change and the fixed second mate are as in the cited dependency nodes.

proof.text: The projection equations identify r with pullback.map on e.hom and the two identity maps. Mathlib pullback.map_isIso gives IsIso r. Apply the proved normalized one-map right-adjoint comparison to f,f′,e and to the two second projections with asIso r.

Construct the source isomorphism explicitly by canonical pullback composition and φ. Take the target isomorphism to be ψ at the lifted LgK. The normalized-square theorem supplies their commutation. Arrow.isoMk constructs the required arrow isomorphism, for each hβf.

proof_origin.note: Actual Lean: prove r invertible, construct normalized right-adjoint comparisons, assemble Arrow.isoMk. One remaining square-calculation hole; endpoint existence is proved.
